ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Imaging in pregnancy

A pregnant patient has persistent right lower quadrant pain and concern for appendicitis. Ultrasound is nondiagnostic, she is stable, and MRI is available without a clinically important delay. Which imaging option is appropriate to clarify the diagnosis without ionizing radiation?

  1. Plain abdominal radiography
  2. No further assessment because ultrasound was inconclusive
  3. Repeat ultrasound as the only allowed test regardless of persistence
  4. Abdominal MRI
  5. CT of the abdomen and pelvis
Answer and explanation

Abdominal MRI

MRI is an appropriate next test after nondiagnostic ultrasound in pregnancy when feasible.

Option explanations

Abdominal MRI: MRI is an appropriate next test after nondiagnostic ultrasound in pregnancy when feasible.

CT of the abdomen and pelvis: CT may be needed in some circumstances, but MRI meets the specified radiation-free goal when available without delay.

Plain abdominal radiography: It is not a sensitive test for appendicitis and uses ionizing radiation.

No further assessment because ultrasound was inconclusive: An inconclusive test does not exclude appendicitis.

Repeat ultrasound as the only allowed test regardless of persistence: Repeated nondiagnostic ultrasound must not prevent appropriate further imaging.
